note: M2-12 cross-runtime parity fixture, read by BOTH runtimes: dashboard/test/inst-changes-bound.test.ts (holdings.ts::compareQoqDeltas / sortQoqDeltas / boundQoqDeltas / utf8ByteLength) and tests/test_qoq_parity.py (scripts/measure_inst_derive.py::_sort_qoq_deltas / _bound_qoq_deltas / _dumps / _utf8_len). Codex closeout F2/F4: the equal-key comparator repair and the lone-surrogate serialization repair each existed in both runtimes with NO committed test invoking the Python side, so reverting either would have left the suite green while the runtimes diverged. Every case here is asserted by both.

comparator.name: reflexive_identical_rows
comparator.why: equal value AND equal key must compare 0 — the exact defect (returned 1) that made the order non-total

comparator.name: value_desc_beats_key
comparator.why: larger current value sorts first regardless of key

comparator.name: null_curr_falls_back_to_prev
comparator.why: an exited position with a disclosed prev value outranks one with nothing disclosed

comparator.name: both_undisclosed_tie_breaks_on_key
comparator.why: both fall back to the -1 sentinel, so the key decides

comparator.name: reflexive_both_undisclosed_same_key
comparator.why: the sentinel path must be reflexive too

comparator.name: zero_is_a_disclosed_value_not_absence
comparator.why: 0 is disclosed and outranks the -1 absence sentinel — G3: absence is not zero
